## Study Design, Biomedical Cohorts, and Synthetic Ground-Truth Regimes

We evaluate the `{python} N.n_models_word` benchmarked architectures defined in Chapter 2 across twelve multi-view benchmarks: six real biomedical and clinical cohorts (`ADNI-MCI`, `MultiOmics` [TCGA-BRCA], `TCGA-KIRC`, `Heart`, `Diabetes`, and `mfeat`) and six synthetic generative regimes with known ground-truth latent coordinates $\mathbf{U}^*$ and feature supports $\mathbf{V}_m^*$ (@tbl-benchmark-cohorts). Every model is evaluated across three independent 70/30 stratified or random train/test splits (seeds $42, 43, 44$) across three `nsa_flow` quantile sparsity levels ($q \in \{\text{None}, 0.5, 0.8\}$, `{python} N.n_default_fits` train/test fits), plus `{python} N.n_positive_reruns` paired reruns with non-negative loadings on the three high-dimensional cohorts and a `{python} N.sweep_n`-configuration hyperparameter sweep on `ADNI-MCI` ($N = 1,084$, one seed). To prevent data leakage, all feature standardization (`StandardScaler`), column completeness filtering ($\ge 98\%$), and demographic covariate adjustments (Frisch–Waugh–Lovell residualization [@frisch1933partial; @lovell1963seasonal] of age, biological sex, and education inside `ADNI-MCI`) are fitted strictly within each training split and applied out-of-sample to the held-out test split.

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| label: tbl-benchmark-cohorts
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of the twelve multi-view benchmark cohorts (six clinical/biomedical datasets and six synthetic ground-truth generative regimes). Best out-of-sample scores across seeds 42–44 are computed directly from `deep_ranking_benchmark.csv`."

#| output: asis
import os
import pandas as pd
from tabulate import tabulate

csv_path = "results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_path):
    csv_path = "paper/results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"

df = pd.read_csv(csv_path)
df["Model"] = df["Model"].replace({"Flow-SiMLR-V": "Flow-SiMR-V", "Flow-SiMLR": "Flow-SiMR"})

cohort_meta = [
    ("ADNI-MCI", "Clinical MRI + Cog", 1084, "4 [160, 160, 62, 11]", "CogPC1 R2 (MRI Only)"),
    ("MultiOmics (BRCA)", "Oncology (mRNA/CNV/RPPA)", 822, "3 [200, 150, 150]", "ER Status Accuracy"),
    ("TCGA-KIRC", "Oncology (mRNA/CNV/RPPA)", 467, "3 [200, 150, 150]", "Pathologic Stage Acc"),
    ("Diabetes", "Clinical Chemistries", 442, "2 [5, 5]", "1-Yr Progression R2"),
    ("Heart", "Cardiology Vitals + ECG", 297, "2 [7, 6]", "Coronary Disease Acc"),
    ("mfeat", "Multi-Descriptor Digits", 2000, "4 [76, 64, 6, 47]", "10-Class Accuracy"),
    ("Linear", "Synthetic (50% Sparse ±)", 1000, "3 [100, 80, 60]", "Latent R2 & Support F1"),
    ("Polynomial", "Synthetic (Deg-3 Warped)", 1000, "3 [120, 80, 50]", "Latent R2 & CMC"),
    ("Sine", "Synthetic (Harmonic Warp)", 1000, "3 [120, 80, 50]", "Latent R2 & CMC"),
    ("Shared+Private", "Synthetic (80% Sparse ±)", 1000, "3 [160, 60, 30]", "Latent R2 & Support F1"),
    ("NonnegParts", "Synthetic (66.7% Non-Neg)", 400, "3 [120, 45, 30]", "Dominant Factor R2 & F1"),
    ("NonnegWeak", "Synthetic (80% Non-Neg)", 400, "3 [120, 45, 30]", "Weak Factor u3 R2 & F1"),
]

rows = []
for ds_label, domain, n_subj, views_str, task_str in cohort_meta:
    if "MultiOmics" in ds_label:
        ds_key = "MultiOmics"
    elif ds_label == "NonnegWeak":
        ds_key = "NonnegPartsWeak"
    else:
        ds_key = ds_label
    sub = df[df["Dataset"] == ds_key]
    agg_xv = sub.groupby("Model")["Strictly_Linear_Metric"].mean()
    pca_v = agg_xv["PCA"]
    best_m = agg_xv.idxmax()
    best_v = agg_xv.max()
    rows.append([
        ds_label,
        domain,
        f"{n_subj:,}",
        views_str,
        task_str,
        f"{best_m} ({best_v:.3f} vs PCA {pca_v:.3f})"
    ])

headers = ["Cohort", "Domain / Modality Structure", "N", "Views [p_m]", "Clinical / Task Target", "Best Linear XV vs PCA"]
print(tabulate(rows, headers=headers, tablefmt="pipe"))
```

In `ADNI-MCI` ($N = 1,084$) [@mueller2005; @jack2008alzheimer; @ADNI], Views 0–2 capture $382$ regional structural MRI features from the ANTsPyT1w/ANTsPyMM pipelines: the volumes of 160 hierarchical segmentation labels (View 0: cortical, subcortical, ventricular, white-matter and cerebellar labels), the volume-to-surface-area ratio of the same 160 labels (View 1; for a cortical label it tracks thickness, otherwise it is a shape index), and DiReCT cortical thickness averaged in each of 62 Desikan–Killiany–Tourville (DKT) cortical regions (View 2) [@avants2008symmetric; @avants2011reproducible; @tustison2014large; @desikan2006automated; @klein2012mindboggle; @stone2020longitudinal; @stone2024blast; @Marek2011; @smith2013functional], while View 3 comprises eleven neuropsychological scales (`ADAS11`, `ADAS13`, `ADASQ4` [@rosen1984new], `MMSE` [@folstein1975mini], `CDRSB` [@morris1993clinical], `TRABSCOR` [@reitan1958validity], `FAQ` [@pfeffer1982measurement], and four Rey Auditory Verbal Learning Test sub-scores `RAVLT_immediate`, `RAVLT_learning`, `RAVLT_forgetting`, `RAVLT_perc_forgetting` [@rey1964examen]). Following `Protocol B`, the three MRI views align with the cognitive battery during training, but test-set predictions are generated exclusively from structural MRI. In `MultiOmics` (`TCGA-BRCA`, $N = 822$) [@tcga2012breast] and `TCGA-KIRC` ($N = 467$) [@tcga2013kirc], mRNA expression ($p_1 = 200$), somatic copy-number variation ($p_2 = 150$), and RPPA proteomics ($p_3 = 150$) predict clinical Estrogen Receptor status and pathologic tumor stage, respectively.

## Global 12-Dataset Benchmark: Subspace Capacity vs. Single-Axis Interpretability

Across the $B = 12$ dataset blocks and `{python} N.n_models_word` architectures, block-averaged non-parametric Friedman [@friedman1937use] and Iman–Davenport [@Iman1980] omnibus tests differentiate the `{python} N.n_models_word` models on both the linear subspace probe ($\chi_F^2 =$ `{python} N.fr_lin_chi2`, $p =$ `{python} N.fr_lin_p`; $F_F =$ `{python} N.fr_lin_F`, $p =$ `{python} N.fr_lin_pF`) and the multi-modal consensus probe ($\chi_F^2 =$ `{python} N.fr_u_chi2`, $p =$ `{python} N.fr_u_p`; $F_F =$ `{python} N.fr_u_F`, $p =$ `{python} N.fr_u_pF`; Nemenyi Critical Difference $CD =$ `{python} N.cd` at $\alpha = 0.05$ [@Demsar2006; @Nemenyi1963; @benavoli2016should]). @tbl-global-leaderboard summarizes the global metrics across all `{python} N.n_models_word` models, accompanied by the Demšar Critical Difference diagram (@fig-cd-diagram), the multi-objective speed–accuracy and support–consensus Pareto frontiers (@fig-pareto-frontier), and the three-probe performance profile (@fig-three-probes).

```{python}
import os
import sys
import pandas as pd
from tabulate import tabulate

csv_main = "results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_main):
    csv_main = "paper/results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"

csv_op = "results_cache/operating_points_05_08_benchmark.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_op):
    csv_op = "paper/results_cache/operating_points_05_08_benchmark.csv"

df_main = pd.read_csv(csv_main)
df_main["Model"] = df_main["Model"].replace({"Flow-SiMLR-V": "Flow-SiMR-V", "Flow-SiMLR": "Flow-SiMR"})

from paper_numbers import op_default
df_op = op_default()  # default positivity only; the paired positive reruns would double-weight 3 cohorts
sub05 = df_op[df_op["Sparseness_Target"] == 0.5]

repo_root = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "..")) if "paper" in os.getcwd() else os.getcwd()
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(repo_root, "src"))
from pysimlr.benchmarks.deep_ranking import build_ranking_blocks, friedman_test

piv_xv, _ = build_ranking_blocks(df_main, metric_col="Strictly_Linear_Metric", floor_threshold=None)
f_xv = friedman_test(piv_xv.values, higher_is_better=True)
ranks_xv = pd.Series(f_xv["mean_ranks"], index=piv_xv.columns)

syn_df = sub05[sub05["Case_Type"] == "synthetic"]
syn_f1 = syn_df.groupby("Model")["Support_Recovery_V"].mean()
syn_cmc = df_main[df_main["Case_Type"] == "synthetic"].groupby("Model")["CMC_Latent_U"].mean()

agg05 = sub05.groupby("Model").agg({
    "Strictly_Linear_Metric": "mean",
    "Axis_Sensitive_Metric": "mean",
    "Predictive_Metric": "mean",
    "Sparsity_Ratio": "mean",
    "Fit_Seconds": "mean"
})

order = ranks_xv.sort_values().index.tolist()
rows = []
for m in order:
    lin_v = agg05.loc[m, "Strictly_Linear_Metric"]
    rf_v = agg05.loc[m, "Axis_Sensitive_Metric"]
    u_v = agg05.loc[m, "Predictive_Metric"]
    drop_v = rf_v - lin_v
    rows.append([
        m,
        f"{ranks_xv[m]:.2f}",
        f"{lin_v:.3f}",
        f"{rf_v:.3f} ({drop_v:+.3f})",
        f"{u_v:.3f}",
        f"{syn_cmc[m]:.3f}",
        f"{syn_f1[m]:.3f}",
        f"{agg05.loc[m, 'Sparsity_Ratio']*100:.1f}%"
    ])

headers = [
    "Architecture", "Friedman Rank ↓", "Linear XV ↑", "RF Axis XV (Drop) ↑",
    "Consensus U ↑", "Latent CMC ↑", "Support F1 ↑", "Sparsity % ↑"
]
print(tabulate(rows, headers=headers, tablefmt="pipe"))
```

```{python}
#| warning: false

#| fig-cap: "Demšar (2006) Critical Difference diagram across the $B = 12$ benchmark dataset blocks (seeds averaged within each dataset) for the linear entrypoint probe ($\\mathbf{X}\\mathbf{V}$; Friedman and Iman–Davenport statistics in the text). Horizontal axis plots mean rank (lower is better, $1 =$ best). Bold horizontal bars connect cliques of architectures whose rank differences are smaller than the Nemenyi Critical Difference ($\\alpha = 0.05$). Green stars (`*`) indicate models on the 5-objective non-dominated Pareto frontier."
#| out-width: 100%
#| echo: false
import os
import sys
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

csv_main = "results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_main):
    csv_main = "paper/results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"

df_main = pd.read_csv(csv_main)
df_main["Model"] = df_main["Model"].replace({"Flow-SiMLR-V": "Flow-SiMR-V", "Flow-SiMLR": "Flow-SiMR"})

repo_root = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "..")) if "paper" in os.getcwd() else os.getcwd()
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(repo_root, "src"))
from pysimlr.benchmarks.deep_ranking import build_ranking_blocks, friedman_test, compute_nemenyi_cd, compute_pareto_frontier
from pysimlr.plotting import theme, VIEW_COLORS

piv_xv, _ = build_ranking_blocks(df_main, metric_col="Strictly_Linear_Metric", floor_threshold=None)
f_xv = friedman_test(piv_xv.values, higher_is_better=True)
ranks = pd.Series(f_xv["mean_ranks"], index=piv_xv.columns).sort_values()
cd = compute_nemenyi_cd(piv_xv.shape[1], piv_xv.shape[0])

agg_all = df_main.groupby("Model", as_index=False).agg({
    "Predictive_Metric": "mean",
    "Strictly_Linear_Metric": "mean",
    "CMC_Latent_U": "mean",
    "Support_Recovery_V": "mean",
    "Fit_Seconds": "mean"
})
pareto_df = compute_pareto_frontier(
    agg_all,
    objectives=["Predictive_Metric", "Strictly_Linear_Metric", "CMC_Latent_U", "Support_Recovery_V", "Fit_Seconds"],
    maximize=[True, True, True, True, False]
)
pareto_set = set(pareto_df[pareto_df["is_pareto_optimal"]]["Model"])
n_m = len(ranks)

with theme():
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10.5, 3.6), dpi=300)
    ax.set_xlim(0.15, n_m + 0.85)
    ax.set_ylim(0.0, 1.25)
    ax.axis("off")

    # Number line 1..n_m
    y_axis = 0.92
    ax.plot([1, n_m], [y_axis, y_axis], color="#0b0b0b", lw=1.4)
    for r_tick in range(1, n_m + 1):
        ax.plot([r_tick, r_tick], [y_axis - 0.035, y_axis + 0.035], color="#0b0b0b", lw=1.1)
        ax.text(r_tick, y_axis + 0.06, str(r_tick), ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=9.5, weight="semibold", color="#0b0b0b")

    # Nemenyi CD reference bar at top left
    cd_x0 = 1.0
    cd_y = 1.15
    ax.plot([cd_x0, cd_x0 + cd], [cd_y, cd_y], color="#e34948", lw=2.2)
    ax.plot([cd_x0, cd_x0], [cd_y - 0.03, cd_y + 0.03], color="#e34948", lw=1.5)
    ax.plot([cd_x0 + cd, cd_x0 + cd], [cd_y - 0.03, cd_y + 0.03], color="#e34948", lw=1.5)
    ax.text(cd_x0 + cd / 2, cd_y + 0.035, f"Nemenyi CD = {cd:.2f} (α = 0.05)", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=9.0, weight="semibold", color="#e34948")

    # Split models into left and right
    n_left = (n_m + 1) // 2
    left_models = list(ranks.index[:n_left])
    right_models = list(ranks.index[n_left:])

    y_positions_left = np.linspace(0.60, 0.12, len(left_models))
    for idx_m, m in enumerate(left_models):
        r_val = ranks[m]
        y_m = y_positions_left[idx_m]
        is_p = m in pareto_set
        col_m = "#0ca30c" if is_p else "#0b0b0b"
        star = " *" if is_p else ""
        ax.plot([r_val, r_val], [y_axis, y_m], color="#898781", lw=0.9, linestyle="-")
        ax.plot([r_val, 0.85], [y_m, y_m], color="#898781", lw=0.9, linestyle="-")
        ax.plot(r_val, y_axis, "o", color=col_m, markeredgecolor="#fcfcfb", markeredgewidth=1.2, markersize=7.0)
        ax.text(0.80, y_m, f"{m}{star} ({r_val:.2f})", ha="right", va="center", fontsize=9.0, weight="semibold", color=col_m)

    y_positions_right = np.linspace(0.60, 0.18, len(right_models))
    for idx_m, m in enumerate(right_models):
        r_val = ranks[m]
        y_m = y_positions_right[idx_m]
        is_p = m in pareto_set
        col_m = "#0ca30c" if is_p else "#0b0b0b"
        star = " *" if is_p else ""
        ax.plot([r_val, r_val], [y_axis, y_m], color="#898781", lw=0.9, linestyle="-")
        ax.plot([r_val, n_m + 0.15], [y_m, y_m], color="#898781", lw=0.9, linestyle="-")
        ax.plot(r_val, y_axis, "o", color=col_m, markeredgecolor="#fcfcfb", markeredgewidth=1.2, markersize=7.0)
        ax.text(n_m + 0.20, y_m, f"({r_val:.2f}) {m}{star}", ha="left", va="center", fontsize=9.0, weight="semibold", color=col_m)

    # Clique bars
    r_vals = ranks.values
    cliques = []
    for i in range(len(r_vals)):
        j = i
        while j + 1 < len(r_vals) and (r_vals[j + 1] - r_vals[i]) <= cd:
            j += 1
        if j > i:
            is_sub = any(c_i <= i and j <= c_j for c_i, c_j in cliques)
            if not is_sub:
                cliques.append((i, j))

    clique_y_base = 0.81
    for c_idx, (i, j) in enumerate(cliques):
        cy = clique_y_base - c_idx * 0.065
        ax.plot([r_vals[i], r_vals[j]], [cy, cy], color="#0b0b0b", lw=3.6, solid_capstyle="round")

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
```

```{python}
import os
import sys
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

csv_main = "results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_main):
    csv_main = "paper/results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"

df_main = pd.read_csv(csv_main)
df_main["Model"] = df_main["Model"].replace({"Flow-SiMLR-V": "Flow-SiMR-V", "Flow-SiMLR": "Flow-SiMR"})

repo_root = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "..")) if "paper" in os.getcwd() else os.getcwd()
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(repo_root, "src"))
from pysimlr.benchmarks.deep_ranking import compute_pareto_frontier
from pysimlr.plotting import theme, VIEW_COLORS

agg_all = df_main.groupby("Model", as_index=False).agg({
    "Predictive_Metric": "mean",
    "Strictly_Linear_Metric": "mean",
    "CMC_Latent_U": "mean",
    "Support_Recovery_V": "mean",
    "Fit_Seconds": "mean"
})
p_df = compute_pareto_frontier(
    agg_all,
    objectives=["Predictive_Metric", "Strictly_Linear_Metric", "CMC_Latent_U", "Support_Recovery_V", "Fit_Seconds"],
    maximize=[True, True, True, True, False]
).set_index("Model")
syn_sub = df_main[df_main["Case_Type"] == "synthetic"].groupby("Model")[["CMC_Latent_U", "Support_Recovery_V"]].mean()

with theme():
    fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11.2, 4.3), dpi=300, constrained_layout=True)

    # Panel A: Consensus U vs Fit_Seconds
    for m, row in p_df.iterrows():
        is_p = bool(row["is_pareto_optimal"])
        marker = "*" if is_p else "o"
        sz = 150 if is_p else 75
        col = "#0ca30c" if is_p else VIEW_COLORS[0]
        ax1.scatter(row["Fit_Seconds"], row["Predictive_Metric"], marker=marker, s=sz, color=col, edgecolor="#fcfcfb", lw=1.2, zorder=4)

    offsets_a = {
        "PCA": (-28, -3),
        "NSAFlow-PCA": (8, 5),
        "SiMLR": (8, -4),
        "LEND": (-14, 9),
        "NED": (-28, -10),
        "NEDPP": (8, 4),
        "Flow-SiMR-V": (-62, -14),
    }
    for m, row in p_df.iterrows():
        dx, dy = offsets_a.get(m, (6, 4))
        col_t = "#0b0b0b" if row["is_pareto_optimal"] else "#52514e"
        ax1.annotate(m, (row["Fit_Seconds"], row["Predictive_Metric"]), xytext=(dx, dy), textcoords="offset points", fontsize=8.4, weight="semibold", color=col_t)

    front_a = p_df.loc[RAW["pareto_2d_models"]]
    ax1.plot(front_a["Fit_Seconds"], front_a["Predictive_Metric"], "--", color="#0ca30c", lw=1.6, alpha=0.85, label="2D Speed–Accuracy Envelope")

    ax1.set_xscale("log")
    ax1.set_xlim(0.005, 35.0)
    ax1.set_ylim(0.61, 0.765)
    ax1.set_xlabel("Mean Fit Time in Seconds (Log Scale, ↓ Faster)")
    ax1.set_ylabel("Out-of-Sample Consensus Score (U ↑)")
    ax1.set_title("A. Consensus Accuracy vs. Fit Time")
    ax1.grid(True)
    ax1.legend(loc="lower left")

    # Panel B: Support F1 vs CMC on Synthetic Regimes
    for m in syn_sub.index:
        is_p = bool(p_df.loc[m, "is_pareto_optimal"])
        marker = "*" if is_p else "o"
        sz = 150 if is_p else 75

    offsets_b = {

        "NED": (-30, -3),
        "NEDPP": (7, 4),
        "Flow-SiMR-V": (8, -6),
        "PCA": (8, 4),
    }
    for m in syn_sub.index:
        dx, dy = offsets_b.get(m, (6, 4))
        col_t = "#0b0b0b" if p_df.loc[m, "is_pareto_optimal"] else "#52514e"
        ax2.annotate(m, (syn_sub.loc[m, "CMC_Latent_U"], syn_sub.loc[m, "Support_Recovery_V"]), xytext=(dx, dy), textcoords="offset points", fontsize=8.4, weight="semibold", color=col_t)

    ax2.set_xlim(0.32, 0.95)

    ax2.set_ylabel("Pathway Support Recovery on V (Jaccard F1 ↑)")
    ax2.set_title("B. Sparse Support Recovery vs. Latent Manifold CMC")
    ax2.grid(True)

    plt.show()
```

```{python}
import os
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pysimlr

csv_main = "results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_main):
    csv_main = "paper/results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"

df_main = pd.read_csv(csv_main)
df_main["Model"] = df_main["Model"].replace({"Flow-SiMLR-V": "Flow-SiMR-V", "Flow-SiMLR": "Flow-SiMR"})
df_blocks = df_main.groupby(["Model", "Dataset"], as_index=False)["Strictly_Linear_Metric"].mean()
model_ord = ["Flow-SiMR-V", "LEND", "SiMLR", "NEDPP", "NED", "PCA", "NSAFlow-PCA"]
df_blocks["Model"] = pd.Categorical(df_blocks["Model"], categories=model_ord, ordered=True)
df_blocks = df_blocks.sort_values(["Model", "Dataset"])
df_blocks["Model"] = df_blocks["Model"].astype(str)

fig = pysimlr.plot_benchmark_uncertainty(
    df_blocks,
    method="Model",
    split="Dataset",
    score="Strictly_Linear_Metric",
    baseline="PCA",
    metric_label="linear entrypoint score (XV)",
)
plt.show()
```


Three empirical principles emerge from @tbl-global-leaderboard and Figures [-@fig-cd-diagram]–[-@fig-three-probes]:

1. **Multi-View Alignment Against Single-Matrix Factorization**: The leading mean Friedman ranks on the linear entrypoint probe are `{python} N.rank_lin_top4`, against `PCA` (`{python} N.rank_lin_PCA`) and `NSAFlow-PCA` (`{python} N.rank_lin_NSAFlow_PCA`) (@fig-benchmark-uncertainty). On heterogeneous cohorts such as `mfeat` ($p = [76, 64, 6, 47]$) and `Shared+Private` ($p = [160, 60, 30]$), concatenated `PCA` reaches a linear score of `{python} N.mfeat_pca` (`mfeat` accuracy) and `{python} N.sp_pca` (`Shared+Private` $R^2$), against `{python} N.mfeat_best` (`{python} N.mfeat_best_model`) and `{python} N.sp_best` (`{python} N.sp_best_model`) for the best multi-view model. Over the 12 datasets (seeds averaged, Wilcoxon signed-rank against `PCA` with Holm adjustment, Appendix B), the linear score differs from `PCA` at $p < 0.05$ for `{python} N.wilcoxon_n_sig` of 6 models (`{python} N.wilcoxon_sig`).
2. **Coordinate Alignment and the Random Forest Axis Drop**: As established in @eq-subspace-invariance, ridge regression on $\mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m$ is insensitive to orthogonal or oblique column mixing $\mathbf{V}_m \mathbf{M}$, hiding the fact that dense `PCA` mixes distinct mechanisms across columns. With coordinate-splitting decision trees (`RandomForest`), `PCA` loses `{python} N.drop_pca` on average across the 12 cohorts (Random Forest minus linear score), falling from `{python} N.npw_pca` to `{python} N.npw_pca_rf` on the weak sparse factors of `NonnegPartsWeak` and from `{python} N.adni_pca` to `{python} N.adni_pca_rf` on `ADNI-MCI` (`{python} N.adni_pca_rf_drop_pct` lower). The smallest drops are `{python} N.drop_best_models`.
3. **Operating Points and Feature Density ($q = 0.5$ vs. $q = 0.8$)**: @fig-operating-point-and-support shows the quantile threshold $q$ as a lens on feature support recovery without conflating scales on secondary axes. Across the `{python} N.n_default_fits` default-positivity fits, the mean linear score is `{python} N.op_lin_None`, `{python} N.op_lin_05` and `{python} N.op_lin_08` at $q = \text{None}$, $0.5$ and $0.8$, and the mean Random Forest axis score is `{python} N.op_rf_None`, `{python} N.op_rf_05` and `{python} N.op_rf_08`; at $q = 0.8$, `{python} N.op_sparsity_08` of loadings are zero while `{python} N.op_retained_08` of the best linear score is retained. At $q = 0.5$, support recovery on the $50\%$-sparse `Linear` regime ranges from $F_1 =$ `{python} N.f1_linear_q05_min` (`{python} N.f1_linear_q05_min_model`) to `{python} N.f1_linear_q05_max` (`{python} N.f1_linear_q05_max_model`), and reaches `{python} N.f1_np_q05_best` on `NonnegParts` (`{python} N.f1_np_q05_best_model`). On the focal $20\%$-active modules, the best $F_1$ at $q = 0.8$ is `{python} N.f1_npw_q08_best` on `NonnegPartsWeak` (`{python} N.f1_npw_q08_best_model`) and `{python} N.f1_sp_q08_best` on `Shared+Private` (`{python} N.f1_sp_q08_best_model`).

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pysimlr
from paper_numbers import op_default

df = op_default().copy()
def _q_lbl(v):
    if pd.isna(v) or str(v) == "None":
        return "q = None"
    return f"q = {float(v):.1f}"

df["Operating point"] = df["Sparseness_Target"].map(_q_lbl)
q_cats = ["q = None", "q = 0.5", "q = 0.8"]

blk_q = df.groupby(["Operating point", "Dataset", "Model"], as_index=False)[
    ["Strictly_Linear_Metric", "Axis_Sensitive_Metric"]
].mean()
long_q = blk_q.melt(
    id_vars=["Operating point", "Dataset", "Model"],
    value_vars=["Strictly_Linear_Metric", "Axis_Sensitive_Metric"],
    var_name="Probe",
    value_name="Score",
)
long_q["Probe"] = long_q["Probe"].map({
    "Strictly_Linear_Metric": "Ridge(XV)",
    "Axis_Sensitive_Metric": "RandomForest(XV)",
})
long_q["Operating point"] = pd.Categorical(long_q["Operating point"], categories=q_cats, ordered=True)
long_q = long_q.sort_values(["Probe", "Operating point"])
long_q["Operating point"] = long_q["Operating point"].astype(object)

syn_q = df[df["Dataset"].isin(["Linear", "NonnegParts", "NonnegPartsWeak", "Shared+Private"])].copy()
syn_q["Operating point"] = pd.Categorical(syn_q["Operating point"], categories=q_cats, ordered=True)
syn_q = syn_q.sort_values(["Dataset", "Operating point"])
syn_q["Operating point"] = syn_q["Operating point"].astype(object)

fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11.6, 4.2), dpi=200, layout="constrained")
pysimlr.plot_benchmark(long_q, x="Operating point", y="Score", by="Probe", kind="line", ax=ax1)
ax1.set_xlim(-0.15, 2.75)
ax1.set_ylabel("Out-of-sample score (↑)")

pysimlr.plot_benchmark(syn_q, x="Operating point", y="Support_Recovery_V", by="Dataset", kind="line", ax=ax2)

ax2.set_ylabel("Pathway support recovery F1 (↑)")
```

## Clinical Neuroimaging in `ADNI-MCI` ($N = 1,084$): Predicting Cognition from MRI Alone and Attributing the Prediction

A primary clinical test of multi-modal representation learning is whether aligning structural neuroimaging with multi-domain cognitive batteries during training yields an anatomical basis that better predicts cognitive severity in new patients who have only undergone an MRI scan (`Protocol B`). Across $N = 1,084$ participants with Mild Cognitive Impairment, @tbl-adni-mci-summary compares all `{python} N.n_models_word` benchmark models on held-out MRI-only prediction of composite cognitive impairment (`CogPC1` $R^2$, after in-fold adjustment for age, sex, and education), single-axis Random Forest prediction, and mean ridge regression $R^2$ across all eleven individual neuropsychological scales (`ADAS11`, `ADAS13`, `ADASQ4`, `MMSE`, `CDRSB`, `TRABSCOR`, `FAQ`, and four `RAVLT` memory scales).

```{python}
agg = sub_adni.groupby("Model").agg({

    sw_11 = best_sw.loc[m, "Mean11_RidgeCV"] if m in best_sw.index else float("nan")
    rows.append([

headers = [
    "Architecture", "3-Seed MRI Linear R2 ↑", "MRI RF Axis R2 ↑",

]
print(tabulate(rows, headers=headers, tablefmt="pipe"))
```

Comparing the unsupervised anatomical baselines against cognitive-aligned SiMR models in @tbl-adni-mci-summary and Figures [-@fig-adni-view-chord]–[-@fig-adni-scores] yields four findings:

1. **Supervising MRI Factor Discovery with Cognitive Batteries Improves Out-of-Sample MRI Prediction**: Unsupervised `PCA` on the $382$ structural MRI features explains $R^2 =$ `{python} N.adni_pca` $\pm$ `{python} N.adni_pca_sd` of out-of-sample cognitive variance (`CogPC1`) on the linear probe and `{python} N.adni_pca_rf` on the single-axis Random Forest probe. Aligning the MRI projections with the 11-scale cognitive battery during training gives, for the four leading models (3-seed means $\pm$ SD), `{python} N.adni_ranked`; the best is `{python} N.adni_gain_pct` over `PCA`. The best single-axis Random Forest score is `{python} N.adni_rf_best` (`{python} N.adni_rf_best_model`), `{python} N.adni_rf_ratio` times that of `PCA`. In the single-seed sweep the best configuration reaches `{python} N.sweep_best_r2` (`{python} N.sweep_best_model`) and the best linear-family configuration `{python} N.sweep_linear_best_r2` (`{python} N.sweep_linear_best_model`), against `{python} N.sweep_pca_r2` for `PCA`; mean prediction across all eleven scales reaches `{python} N.sweep_m11_best` (`{python} N.sweep_m11_best_model`) against `{python} N.sweep_m11_pca` for `PCA` (`{python} N.sweep_m11_gain`). These sweep peaks are maxima over many configurations on one split and are optimistic.
2. **Which MRI Features Carry the Prediction**: @fig-adni-neuroanatomy-flagship attributes the held-out `CogPC1` prediction of the non-negative $q = 0.85$ fit (all nine MRI columns, $R^2 =$ `{python} N.attr_full_r2`). Component 2 carries it in every MRI view: alone it gives $R^2 =$ `{python} N.attr_vol_c2_r2` (volume), `{python} N.attr_va_c2_r2` (vol/area) and `{python} N.attr_dkt_c2_r2` (DiReCT thickness), against at most `{python} N.attr_dkt_c3_r2` for any other column, and only the vol/area column is not redundant with the rest (unique $R^2$ `{python} N.attr_va_c2_unique`). Across `{python} N.attr_n_halves` half-sample refits, the vol/area component-2 basis selects these features in at least half of them (fraction of refits): `{python} N.attr_cur_va_top`. These are mostly entorhinal, temporal-lobe and inferior parietal measures, the regions where atrophy is expected in prodromal Alzheimer's disease [@dickerson2009cortical; @jack2018nia]. DiReCT thickness tells the same story less clearly. Its first principal component explains `{python} N.attr_dkt_pc1` of the variance across the 62 regions (mean inter-region correlation `{python} N.attr_dkt_mean_corr`), and consensus component 2 correlates `{python} N.attr_c2_global_r` with subject-mean thickness, so hard-assigning each region to its largest structure coefficient places `{python} N.attr_hard_counts` regions on components 1 / 2 / 3: a display of the global factor, not of localisation (Panel B). The thickness basis itself is unstable under the default collapse penalty: it keeps two or fewer regions in `{python} N.attr_cur_dkt_degenerate` of `{python} N.attr_n_halves` refits (median held-out $R^2$ `{python} N.attr_cur_dkt_med_r2`). Non-negative region sums on positively correlated features typically correlate above the penalty's threshold of 0.3, so the penalty pushes those columns towards one or two regions. With `collapse_weight = 0` the predictive thickness basis keeps a median of `{python} N.attr_nc_dkt_med_n` regions (two or fewer in `{python} N.attr_nc_dkt_degenerate` refit), its median $R^2$ rises to `{python} N.attr_nc_dkt_med_r2`, and its most frequent regions are (fraction of refits) `{python} N.attr_nc_dkt_top` (Panel D). No single thickness region replicates in more than `{python} N.attr_nc_dkt_top_max` of refits, so the thickness map is a pattern, not a list of identified regions (`docs/audit/evidence/adni_global_factor_check.csv`). For reference, unthresholded non-negative fits are `{python} N.fl_col_pca_simr_sp` sparse on the DKT view without rotation and `{python} N.fl_varimax_simr_sp` with Varimax, against `{python} N.fl_pca_sp` for dense `PCA`.
3. **Support-Shuffled and PCA-Rotated Score Controls**: To separate coordinate-level axis alignment and anatomical support localization from subspace capacity, two negative controls are evaluated across 3 seeds on `ADNI-MCI` (`adni_mci_axis_alignment_controls.csv`, `axis_alignment_control_metrics`): (i) a **PCA-Rotated Score Control** rotates the learned scores $\mathbf{Z} = [\mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m]$ by their in-fold principal-component eigenvectors, which leaves the linear probe unchanged (largest difference `{python} N.ctl_linear_invariance`) and lowers the single-axis Random Forest score for `{python} N.ctl_rot_n_lower` of `{python} N.ctl_n_models` models; (ii) a **Support-Shuffled Basis Control** permutes the rows of each $\mathbf{V}_m$ within its view, preserving sparsity, weight magnitudes and $\mathbf{V}_m^\top \mathbf{V}_m$, and lowers the Random Forest `CogPC1` $R^2$ for `{python} N.ctl_shuffle_n_lower` of `{python} N.ctl_n_models` models: `{python} N.ctl_shuffle_lowers`. Unshuffled Random Forest scores are `{python} N.ctl_rf_ratio_min`–`{python} N.ctl_rf_ratio_max` times that of `PCA`.
4. **Rank Selection, Component Identifiability, and Display Policy**: Evaluating latent rank selection via `select_rank` across 20 half-sample refits (`adni_rank_selection.csv`) reveals that component identifiability depends critically on rank $k$ and non-negativity. At $k = 3$ under non-negativity, component stabilities are `{python} N.adni_k3_pos_stab_c1` ($0.975$), `{python} N.adni_k3_pos_stab_c2` ($0.803$), and `{python} N.adni_k3_pos_stab_c3` ($0.996$). Component 2 is unstable ($0.803 < 0.90$) and therefore classified as **not identified** (`all_stable=False`). In contrast, at $k = 2$ under positivity, both components achieve full stability and identifiability (`all_stable=True`, stabilities `{python} N.adni_k2_pos_stab_c1` [$0.961$] and `{python} N.adni_k2_pos_stab_c2` [$0.997$]). Under signed estimation (`positivity="either"`), stabilities at $k = 3$ drop to `{python} N.adni_k3_either_stab_c1` ($0.993$), `{python} N.adni_k3_either_stab_c2` ($0.568$), and `{python} N.adni_k3_either_stab_c3` ($0.792$), failing identification on components 2 and 3.
   * **Signed Displays Protocol**: Across all displays in this manuscript: (i) feature maps display only features whose 95% bootstrap confidence interval (from whole-pipeline refits in `loading_inference`) strictly excludes zero; (ii) named biomarker panels report features selected via Meinshausen–Bühlmann stability selection at threshold $\pi_{\text{thr}} = 0.80$ with expected false selections $E[\text{false}] \le 1.0$; and (iii) non-negative displays present hard-assignment OLEE loadings accompanied by the `loading_margin` certainty metric.

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pysimlr

def _dkt_lobe(nm):
    s = nm.replace("left_", "").replace("right_", "")
    if any(k in s for k in ("entorhinal", "fusiform", "parahippocampal", "temporal")):
        return "Temporal"
    if any(k in s for k in ("cingulate",)):
        return "Cingulate"
    if any(k in s for k in ("parietal", "precuneus", "supramarginal", "postcentral")):
        return "Parietal"
    if any(k in s for k in ("cuneus", "occipital", "lingual", "pericalcarine")):
        return "Occipital"
    if "insula" in s:
        return "Insula"
    return "Frontal"

_dkt_groups = [_dkt_lobe(nm) for nm in _d_adni["names"][2]]
_all_adni_names = list(_d_adni["names"]) + [[f"cog_{i}" for i in range(_d_adni["y_tr"].shape[1])]]
fig = pysimlr.plot_feature_groups(
    _res_adni,
    _dkt_groups,
    view=2,
    feature_names=_all_adni_names,
    statistic="mean_abs",
    view_names=_adni_vnames,
)
plt.show()
```

## Multi-Omic Oncology (`TCGA-BRCA`, `TCGA-KIRC`) and Patient-Level Clinical Attribution

To verify that the same architectural principles generalize beyond neuroimaging to molecular oncology and clinical tabular medicine, @tbl-real-cohorts-summary compares all `{python} N.n_models_word` models across the six real cohorts, @fig-multiomics-and-patient-attribution reports cross-cohort linear entrypoint scores (`pysimlr.plot_benchmark`), @fig-diabetes-top-features and @fig-heart-audit map reproducible feature-to-component structure (`pysimlr.plot_top_features` and `pysimlr.plot_feature_chord`), and @fig-nsa-v-interpretability displays the hard-assigned OLEE loadings $\mathbf{L}_m$ across `Heart` and `Diabetes` modalities.

```{python}

#| message: false
#| label: tbl-real-cohorts-summary

import os
import pandas as pd
from tabulate import tabulate

df["Model"] = df["Model"].replace({"Flow-SiMLR-V": "Flow-SiMR-V", "Flow-SiMLR": "Flow-SiMR"})

models = ["LEND", "Flow-SiMR-V", "SiMLR", "NEDPP", "NED", "NSAFlow-PCA", "PCA"]

    for ds in real_dsets:
        sub = df[(df["Dataset"] == ds) & (df["Model"] == m)]

headers = [
    "Architecture", "ADNI-MCI R2 ↑", "TCGA-BRCA Acc ↑", "TCGA-KIRC Acc ↑",
    "Diabetes R2 ↑", "Heart Acc ↑", "mfeat Acc ↑"
]
print(tabulate(rows, headers=headers, tablefmt="pipe"))
```

```{python}
from pysimlr.plotting import theme, _header

csv_path = "results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_path):

df = pd.read_csv(csv_path)
df["Model"] = df["Model"].replace({"Flow-SiMLR-V": "Flow-SiMR-V", "Flow-SiMLR": "Flow-SiMR"})
real_map = {
    "ADNI-MCI": "ADNI-MCI (R²)",
    "MultiOmics": "TCGA-BRCA (Acc)",
    "TCGA-KIRC": "TCGA-KIRC (Acc)",
    "Diabetes": "Diabetes (R²)",
    "Heart": "Heart (Acc)",
    "mfeat": "mfeat (Acc)",
}
sub_r = df[df["Dataset"].isin(real_map.keys()) & df["Model"].isin(["LEND", "Flow-SiMR-V", "SiMLR", "PCA"])].copy()
sub_r["Cohort"] = pd.Categorical(sub_r["Dataset"].map(real_map), categories=list(real_map.values()), ordered=True)
sub_r["Model"] = pd.Categorical(sub_r["Model"], categories=["LEND", "Flow-SiMR-V", "SiMLR", "PCA"], ordered=True)
sub_r = sub_r.sort_values(["Cohort", "Model"])
sub_r["Cohort"] = sub_r["Cohort"].astype(object)
sub_r["Model"] = sub_r["Model"].astype(object)

with theme():
    fig, ax1 = plt.subplots(figsize=(10.2, 4.3), dpi=300, layout="constrained")
    pysimlr.plot_benchmark(sub_r, x="Cohort", y="Strictly_Linear_Metric", by="Model", kind="bar", ax=ax1)
    ax1.set_xlabel("")
    ax1.set_ylabel("Out-of-sample linear probe score (↑)")
    ax1.set_title("")
    _header(fig, "Multi-cohort out-of-sample linear entrypoint scores",
            "3-seed mean ± SE across six real cohorts · higher is better")
    plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-nsa-v-interpretability
#| echo: false
#| out-width: 100%
#| fig-cap: "**Hierarchical Sparse Basis Localization (`nsa_flow`).** `LEND` OLEE loadings $\\mathbf{L}_m$ of each `Heart` and `Diabetes` view (`results_cache/nsa_v_loadings.json`); G is the Gini coefficient of each component and average loading margins are reported."
import json, os
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from paper_numbers import CACHE
from pysimlr.plotting import theme, _cmap, _matrix, _header

NSAV = json.load(open(os.path.join(CACHE, "nsa_v_loadings.json")))

def _gini(x):
    x = np.sort(np.abs(np.asarray(x, float)))
    n = len(x)
    return 0.0 if x.sum() == 0 else float(np.sum((2 * np.arange(1, n + 1) - n - 1) * x) / (n * x.sum()))

with theme():
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(8.8, 8.6), dpi=300, layout="constrained")
    for ax, (cohort, view) in zip(axes.ravel(), [(c, v) for c in ("Heart", "Diabetes") for v in NSAV[c]]):
        d = NSAV[cohort][view]
        v = np.array(d.get("loadings", d.get("v")), float)
        margin = np.array(d["loading_margin"], float) if "loading_margin" in d and d["loading_margin"] is not None else None
        order = np.lexsort((-v.max(1), v.argmax(1), (v.max(1) <= 1e-4).astype(int)))
        v, rows = v[order], [d["rows"][i] for i in order]
        cols = [f"L{j + 1} (G={_gini(v[:, j]):.2f})" for j in range(v.shape[1])]
        _matrix(ax, v, _cmap("seq"), 0.0, 0.95, fmt="{:.2f}", rows=rows, cols=cols)
        margin_str = f" · margin {margin.mean():.2f}" if margin is not None else ""
        ax.set_title(f"{cohort}: {view}{margin_str}", loc="left", fontsize=9.8)
    _header(fig, "OLEE sparse basis loadings",
            "Gini sparsity G and mean winner-vs-runner-up loading margin per view")
    plt.show()
```
:::
::::

In `MultiOmics` (`TCGA-BRCA`, $N = 822$), out-of-sample Estrogen Receptor classification accuracy on the linear entrypoint is `{python} N.brca_Flow_SiMR_V_pm` (`Flow-SiMR-V`), `{python} N.brca_LEND_pm` (`LEND`) and `{python} N.brca_NEDPP_pm` (`NEDPP`), against `{python} N.brca_PCA_pm` for `PCA` (3-seed means $\pm$ SD); the sparse non-negative dictionaries $\mathbf{V}_m$, tri-modal feature chord, and view-level quality radar are examined in Appendix A. In `TCGA-KIRC` ($N = 467$), pathologic stage classification on the consensus embedding $\mathbf{U}$ is `{python} N.kirc_LEND_u_pm` for `LEND` against `{python} N.kirc_PCA_u_pm` for `PCA`. On compact clinical cohorts, `Diabetes` reaches $R^2 =$ `{python} N.diab_SiMLR` for `SiMLR` against `{python} N.diab_pca` for `PCA`, and `Heart` reaches accuracy `{python} N.heart_NSAFlow_PCA` for `NSAFlow-PCA` and `{python} N.heart_SiMLR` for `SiMLR`. @fig-diabetes-top-features, @fig-heart-audit, and @fig-nsa-v-interpretability show the stability-selected structure correlations, multi-view feature-to-component chord, and OLEE loadings $\mathbf{L}_m$ across `Heart` and `Diabetes`; while the linear entrypoint $\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}} = \mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m$ maps individual observations into the latent consensus space, the OLEE loadings $\mathbf{L}_m$ decompose individual patient profiles into exact additive risk attributions $c_{m,i,j,l} = x_{m,i,j} l_{m,j,l}$ without post-hoc Monte Carlo approximations [@Wachter_2017; @karimi2021algorithmic; @pearl2009causality]. Complete parameter sensitivity ablations—the $w \in [0.01, 0.95]$ trade-off curve, basis diagnostics, stability rank selection across $k$, and synthetic noise recovery—are in Appendix B.
